context.guidance: Make the erasure route delete the Personal Data Elements from every store, cache and backup in scope, rather than setting a flag or hiding the records. Include the Data Processors in each erasure request, as §8(7)(b) requires, and confirm completion for each one. Keep only what a legal retention duty obliges you to keep, and erase the rest on request under §12(3).

value.fix: Replace the flag-only handling of deletionRequested: true with a real erasure workflow. When a request arrives, create an erasure job that hard-deletes the Personal Data Elements from every in-scope store, cache, and backup (for backups, purge them on rotation or suppress restoration of erased records). Send an erasure request to each Data Processor, as §8(7)(b) requires, and store each processor's confirmation of completion. Retain only the data that a specific legal retention duty requires, record that legal basis per field, and erase everything else on request under §12(3). Use the flag only as a status marker for the job, not as the erasure mechanism, and add tests that confirm the records are gone from the primary store, caches, and processor copies. I have not checked this against the repository, so the specific files and stores that need changes still need to be identified.
